title: Low-Interaction Honeypots
description: Deploys low-interaction honeypots emulating services to catch scanners and worms. They answer just enough protocol to log the attack; there is no real system to compromise. Cheap and safe, they see the internet's background radiation.

demo.title: Demo — Low-Interaction Honeypots

title: High-Interaction Honeypots
description: Runs full operating systems as high-interaction honeypots to study advanced attackers. Real systems invite real techniques; containment keeps them from escaping. The intelligence is worth the risk when done right.

demo.title: Demo — High-Interaction Honeypots

title: Cowrie SSH Honeypot
description: Runs Cowrie to emulate SSH and Telnet, logging brute-force attacks and intruder commands. It fakes a filesystem convincingly; attackers reveal their toolkits. It is the standard SSH honeypot.

demo.title: Demo — Cowrie SSH Honeypot

title: Traffic Mirroring
description: Mirrors suspicious traffic to honeypots with SPAN ports or taps. Production flows continue untouched while copies go to analysis. It observes without interfering.

demo.title: Demo — Traffic Mirroring

title: SDN Redirection
description: Steers attacker flows to honeypots with SDN rules the moment suspicion crosses a threshold. The attacker never knows the network reprogrammed around them. It is deception at wire speed.

demo.title: Demo — SDN Redirection

title: Tarpit Defenses
description: Slows attackers with tarpits that answer just slowly enough to waste their time. LaBrea-style tarpits hold connections open for hours; scanners crawl. It turns the attacker's parallelism against them.

demo.title: Demo — Tarpit Defenses

title: Deception Grids
description: Deploys coordinated deception grids: fake hosts, credentials, and documents across the network. Attackers cannot tell real from fake; every touch alerts. It makes the whole network hostile terrain.

demo.title: Demo — Deception Grids

title: Attacker Profiling
description: Profiles attackers from honeypot interactions: tools, timing, targets. Profiles feed threat intelligence and tune defenses. Knowing the adversary beats guessing.

demo.title: Demo — Attacker Profiling

title: Alert Correlation
description: Correlates honeypot alerts with IDS, firewall, and EDR events into single incidents. One attacker trips many sensors; correlation assembles the campaign. It cuts alert fatigue.

demo.title: Demo — Alert Correlation

title: Dynamic Honeypot Deployment
description: Spins honeypots up and down automatically where attacks are detected. Orchestration places decoys near the action; idle regions get none. It keeps deception fresh and cheap.

demo.title: Demo — Dynamic Honeypot Deployment

title: Containerized Honeypots
description: Runs honeypots as disposable containers for fast reset and scale. A compromised honeypot is destroyed and respawned clean in seconds. It makes high-interaction honeypots operationally sane.

demo.title: Demo — Containerized Honeypots

title: IoT Honeypots
description: Emulates IoT devices — cameras, routers — to catch botnets like Mirai variants. Telnet and default credentials attract automated attacks; the honeypot logs the payloads. It watches the IoT threat landscape.

demo.title: Demo — IoT Honeypots

title: Credential Canaries
description: Plants fake credentials that alert when used, proving an intruder is active. Canary AWS keys, database logins, and documents sit waiting; any use is malicious by definition. It is the simplest tripwire there is.

demo.title: Demo — Credential Canaries

title: Egress Analysis
description: Analyzes what attackers try to exfiltrate from honeypots. Fake data marked for theft reveals attacker interests when they take the bait. It turns theft into intelligence.

demo.title: Demo — Egress Analysis

title: Deception Legal Review
description: Reviews honeypot deployments with legal counsel for entrapment and privacy issues. Decoys must not induce crimes or collect personal data improperly. The review keeps deception lawful.

demo.title: Demo — Deception Legal Review
